evidence.mission_note: A manual 2001 Z3 3.0i at $11,500 is the profile's main enthusiast-bridge target and sits squarely in the ideal price band. Its fit depends entirely on verifying cooling and rear structure, given Jason is coming off a BMW with a cooling failure.
evidence.rationale: The listing establishes, by photo, a dark-green 2001 Z3 roadster with a 3.0i badge, M54-style engine and straight paint. The manual, 78k miles, clean title and 3+ owners rest only on seller statements. The seller discloses a rear plastic window needing replacement (a new window included), light rock chips, seat wear and top wear. Claimed front control-arm, tie-rod and Delrin work has no receipts, and the only routine maintenance cited is an oil change and filters. Neither model-critical item is evidenced: there is nothing on rear subframe or trunk-floor condition, and nothing on cooling-system age, which matters on an Illinois car at 25 years. A 2023 temp permit in the photos suggests they may be stale, and the ad has been relisted repeatedly since about Sept 2025. The tracker's link to a 28k-mile 2024 Minnesota listing is not VIN-based and should be resolved with the VIN. Price sits about 7% under the fair-value midpoint.
evidence.next_action: Message the seller for the VIN, a title photo, a dated odometer photo, and trunk-floor/subframe and underside photos, and ask whether a PPI at a Chicago-area BMW independent shop is allowed before any deposit.
